tytul: Garlic cloves in vinegar for the refrigerator (UC ANR method)
wstep: This card describes the UC ANR method for storing peeled garlic cloves in undiluted vinegar in the refrigerator.

akapity: Peeled garlic cloves and undiluted (full-strength) vinegar.

For this card JarAtlas follows the Wisconsin Extension rule for quick pickles: use only vinegar labelled 5% acidity; white and cider vinegar are interchangeable; do not use wine vinegars, homemade vinegar or lemon juice.
Vinegar with less than 5% acidity should never be used in home food preservation.
A small amount of dried spices, such as peppercorns, hot chili flakes, cumin seeds or bay leaves, may be added.
Submerge the peeled cloves in the vinegar and store the jar in the refrigerator.
The vinegar gives an acidic environment, with a pH below 4.6, in which Clostridium botulinum cannot grow.
The garlic-flavored vinegar and the cloves may be used to flavor dishes.
The garlic in vinegar should keep for about 4 months in the refrigerator; label the jar with the preparation date and a “best before” date.
Longer storage should not make it unsafe, but mold may develop and the flavor may change.
Do not store it at room temperature, because it rapidly develops mold.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the jar on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door: Wisconsin Extension assumes 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder for refrigerator pickles, while a Polish sanitary inspection office gives about 10 °C for the door, even though it suggests the door for jars of preserves.
If there are signs of mold or yeast growth on the surface of the vinegar, discard both the cloves and the liquid.
